facts.statement: Entradasuchus is a genus of crocodyliform, an early relative of modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: Entradasuchus (meaning "Entrada [Sandstone and Ranch] crocodile") is a genus of crocodyliform, an early member of the group including crocodilians.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Entradasuchus was discovered in the Entrada Sandstone at Entrada Ranch in Grand County, Utah.
facts.quote: The only known specimen was found in rocks of the Middle Jurassic Entrada Sandstone of Entrada Ranch, Grand County, Utah.

facts.statement: Adrian Hunt and Martin Lockley described Entradasuchus in 1995 and initially classified it as Crocodyliformes incertae sedis.
facts.quote: Adrian Hunt and Martin Lockley, who described Entradasuchus in 1995, classified it as Crocodyliformes incertae sedis.

facts.statement: Entradasuchus lived during the very late middle Callovian stage of the Middle Jurassic.
facts.quote: The block containing the specimen weathered from canyon walls and probably came from the middle Moab Member of the Entrada Sandstone, dated to the very late middle Callovian of the Middle Jurassic.

facts.statement: Entradasuchus inhabited an inland dune environment during the Middle Jurassic.
facts.quote: The Moab Member of the Entrada Sandstone represents an inland dune (eolian) setting.

facts.statement: Approximately 42 pairs of armor scutes ran along the midline of Entradasuchus's back.
facts.quote: Approximately 42 pairs of scutes ran down the midline of the back.

facts.statement: The scutes on Entradasuchus's back and tail were rectangular with short spiny projections on their rear corners.
facts.quote: The first pair behind the skull were square, but those on the back and tail were rectangular and had short spiny projections on their posterior outside corners.

facts.statement: The spiny projections on the scutes inspired the specific name spinosus for the type species.
facts.quote: These spines inspired the name of the type species: E. spinosus.

facts.statement: Despite its small size, evidence such as fused parietals suggests that the known specimen of Entradasuchus was an adult.
facts.quote: This small size and the form of the skull could indicate it was a juvenile, but the fusion of the parietals in the skull and the generally small size of animals found in settings like the upper Entrada Sandstone suggest it was an adult.

facts.statement: Entradasuchus lived between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago during the Callovian age.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Callovian (165.3 to 161.5 million years ago)

rejected.statement: When described in 1995, Entradasuchus was the first confirmed North American Middle Jurassic nonmarine tetrapod known from body fossils.
rejected.quote: Entradasuchus was the first unequivocal North American Middle Jurassic nonmarine tetrapod known from body fossils when it was described (1995).

rejected.quote: CU-MWC 183-11 was not a large animal, with a skull only a few centimeters or inches long.
